findings.where: Hero, the handwritten 'Write to me' note in the left margin (desktop); the same note under the hero lines (phone); no footer or contact line anywhere on the tile
findings.fault: The page's one action, getting in touch with Mark, is a small red scribble. On desktop it sits outside the text column, beyond the double margin rule, so it reads like a note someone jotted on the pad and not like a way to reach him. It is a mailto link and the email address never appears in full. 'Contact' in the nav goes nowhere yet (#), and the tile shows no footer with the address, even though the palette assigns the binding colour to a footer.
findings.who_objects: An officer at a development bank who has read the line about the World Bank's PPP Group and wants to write. The scribble may not look like a way to act. If they do click, on a work machine with webmail and no mail app set up, nothing opens, and there is no address on the page to copy. First-visit trust item 7 asks for the address in full as its own link text.

findings.where: Hero, the italic line 'Over 40 years of international infrastructure experience.' under the subheading
findings.fault: The hero's second claim is a size word that nobody can check. It does not say where, for whom or on what kind of project. It also stacks a boast on top of the one strong line above it, the specific World Bank role, and the boast is the weaker of the two.
findings.who_objects: Procurement staff at a development bank. They judge relevant experience by project kind and region, so 'over 40 years' tells them nothing they can weigh, and it reads like the established-firm voice Mark has rejected. Two rules object as well: Feel the CV ('never size words such as "40 years of experience"') and client value 6 (one strong line, no boasts).

findings.where: Hero, the heading and the subheading as a 5-second read
findings.fault: Above the fold, the page says what Mark does and gives one credential. It does not say who he does it for, and it gives no region or country of his work. 'International' is the only word about place.
findings.who_objects: A staff member at a multilateral or bilateral agency who is trying to tell in seconds whether this advisor has worked in their region and for bodies like theirs. That is the first thing a visitor to an advisor's site must be sure of (first-visit trust items 2 and 6). Without it they have to dig, or they leave.

findings.where: Article specimen, the lecture row 'Streamlining the PPP Process … Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF'; the hero, which shows no other proof
findings.fault: Mark's newest talk is listed with no venue and no host. Apart from the past employer, nothing on the page shows that a named body invited, published or hired him. Absent social proof should be reported.
findings.who_objects: A procurement reader who looks for standing shown by who asked. A lecture with no named host proves nothing to them, and Feel the CV asks for the newest talk to be shown with its venue. With no testimonials held, a link out to work hosted by a named body is the only real proof available, and the tile leaves no place for it.
